headline: What Makes a Coding Agent Trustworthy? A Look at SolonCode's Design Choices
summary: With new coding agents emerging weekly, developers question their trustworthiness. This article examines five key design choices, using SolonCode as an open-source example, to help evaluate an agent's reliability with your codebase.
details: Every week, new coding agents emerge, prompting developers to question their trustworthiness with sensitive codebases. This article explores five crucial design choices that build trust, using the open-source SolonCode agent as a practical reference point.

The strongest form of trust comes from transparency. SolonCode is MIT-licensed and fully open source, including its CLI, Web UI, and desktop client. This allows developers to inspect its code and verify exactly what it sends to models and where it stores data.

Crucially, SolonCode runs locally on your machine, interacting directly with your configured model endpoint. There's no mandatory middle-tier service, which is vital for teams with legal restrictions on where their source code can reside.

Many agents are tied to a single model provider, creating dependency issues. SolonCode is provider-agnostic, allowing users to configure any hosted API, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or local model. This flexibility means switching models is a simple configuration change.

Trust also means control over autonomy. SolonCode offers explicit work modes, from read-only planning to full execution with approval. Developers can choose the risk level per task, ensuring they decide how much freedom the agent has.

Even careful agents can make mistakes, so reversibility is key. SolonCode maintains persistent session history with rewind/redo and recoverable workspace checkpoints. This allows developers to roll back to a known-good state if a run goes awry, preventing disasters.

These five principles prioritize verifiable behavior over mere 'smartness.' An agent that can be inspected, run locally, configured with any model, gated with approvals, and easily undone offers a foundation for trust that opaque, smart-only agents cannot.

headline: Panda unveils world's first personal AI computer with 3TB storage, no subscriptions
summary: This device brings AI processing entirely into your home, offering complete privacy and serving up to 25 devices without data centers or subscriptions.
details: Panda is introduced as the world's first personal AI computer, designed for local processing of chat, code, research, and media creation. It features 3 TB of storage, ensuring all data remains on the device within the user's home.

This device aims to replicate the privacy of a traditional calculator, keeping all AI operations, files, and chats entirely private. It plugs into a wall outlet near a Wi-Fi router, with an accompanying app for access.

Panda supports generating illustrations, photos, and 3D models from descriptions. It can serve up to 25 devices simultaneously, allowing multiple users in a home or office to utilize its AI capabilities with full privacy.

The device comes with a suite of integrated business tools, eliminating the need for additional subscriptions or third-party access to user files. It operates in "Local mode" for nearby access and "Live mode" for remote access from anywhere.

Panda is priced at $2,997, with a $100 deposit required to reserve a unit. The remaining $2,897 is charged before shipping, which is scheduled to begin in December 2027 for the first limited run of 1,000 devices.
